title: The canal that split two continents
text: The Panama Canal {{1}} begun by a French company in 1880 under Ferdinand de Lesseps, {{2}} triumph at Suez had made him world famous. But tropical disease killed so many workers {{3}} the venture collapsed in scandal, and the abandoned excavation lay festering until the United States, {{4}} had strategic reasons of its own, took the project over. American engineers chose locks instead {{5}} a sea-level channel, taming the Chagres River with a vast artificial lake, and in 1914 the first ships crossed from the Atlantic {{6}} the Pacific — at {{7}} same moment the First World War was breaking out in Europe. The canal {{8}} is a monument to organisation: every transit is scheduled, every lock is timed, and a century of ships has followed the same giant staircase between the oceans.

gaps.explanation: Past passive with a singular subject: was begun.

gaps.hint: relative: de Lesseps, ___ triumph at Suez
gaps.explanation: 'Whose' links the engineer to his triumph.

gaps.hint: conjunction: so many workers ___ the venture collapsed
gaps.explanation: 'So many … that' — degree plus result clause.

gaps.hint: relative: the United States, ___ had strategic reasons
gaps.explanation: Non-defining relative after the comma referring to the country.

gaps.hint: preposition: locks instead ___ a sea-level channel
preposition: crossed from the Atlantic ___ the Pacific
gaps.explanation: 'From … to …' — the span of the crossing.
'At the same time/moment' is the fixed phrase.

gaps.hint: reflexive: the canal ___ is a monument
